records.name_note: Every admissible source treats "Geranium sanguineum" as the correct, currently accepted binomial — RHS explicitly lists "Name Status: Correct" for it, with no synonym flagged. None of the sources use "hardy geranium" as the plant's own common name; they call it "bloody cranesbill," "bloodred geranium," or "bloody geranium." "Hardy geranium" is a generic nursery-trade term for perennial Geranium species as a group, carried over from the task's naming rather than sourced.
unknowns: toxic_to_pets / toxicity_detail: no admissible source addresses Geranium sanguineum toxicity to pets specifically; the 'toxic houseplant' lists that turned up in search on Clemson/UGA domains cover Pelargonium (the common bedding plant popularly nicknamed 'geranium'), a different genus, so they were not used per the no-genus-inference rule.

chill_damage_f: RHS assigns an H7 cold-hardiness rating ("hardy in the severest European continental climates, < -20C"), but that is a mature-plant winter survival floor, not the temperature at which frost/cold damage begins, so it was not mapped to this field.

water_regime and its day-count fields (water_growing_days_est, water_dormant_days_est, water_estimate_basis, water_check_depth_cm, water_dry_down_target): sources give only a categorical 'Water: Medium' tag and a general 'moist but well-drained soil' preference for this in-ground garden perennial; none frame watering as a container dry-down cycle matching the regime options, and none give any interval or estimate basis, so all were left null rather than invented.

day_f_min/day_f_max, night_f_min/night_f_max: no source gives day or night operating temperature ranges; only a winter cold-hardiness zone/rating exists, which doesn't convert to a day- or night-specific figure.

light_fc_min, light_fc_good, direct_sun_hours_max: sources give only a categorical sun-exposure tag (full sun / part shade); NC State's 'Full sun (6 or more hours...)' wording is that site's standard boilerplate definition of the category, reused across many unrelated plant pages, not a species-specific hour count, so it was captured via outdoor_sun_exposure instead of direct_sun_hours_max.
humidity_need, humidity_pct_min, humidity_pct_max: no source addresses ambient humidity for this outdoor garden perennial.
fertilize_active_months, fertilize_interval_days, fertilize_strength: no source addresses a fertilizing schedule or strength for this species.
cool_rest_note: no source discusses a dormancy or cool-rest period requirement.

soil_drainage — removed on audit: Record set soil_drainage="moderate" citing only NC State's paraphrased prose ("moist but well-drained soil ... tolerates ... some drought"). But NC State's own STRUCTURED attribute field on that same page, literally labeled 'Soil Drainage:', lists this species as 'Good Drainage' and 'Moist' -- not 'moderate'. RHS's structured 'Moisture' field (also categorical, not prose) independently confirms 'Moist but well-drained or Well-drained'. All three admissible sources' own categorical data indicate a well-drained/good-drainage requirement; none support a distinct 'moderate' drainage tier. The record picked a value from a prose paraphrase that contradicts the cited source's own structured field of the same name -- exactly the failure mode structural check #1 warns about.

water_regime — removed on audit: The record sets water_regime='keep_moist' citing only one clause of MOBOT's Culture paragraph ('preference for consistent moisture during the growing season'). But MOBOT's own STRUCTURED summary field for this exact page rates the plant 'Water: Medium' (verified in raw page fetch, alongside Sun/Maintenance/etc. structured fields) — a milder categorical rating than 'keep_moist' implies. The same Culture paragraph the record quotes from also immediately states 'Plants have tolerance for some dry shade once established,' which the citation omits. This is the structured-field-vs-selectively-quoted-prose pattern the audit flags: the record picked the stronger-sounding prose clause and ignored both the source's own structured 'Medium' rating and the drought-tolerance sentence sitting in the same paragraph.

scientific_name_accepted — removed on audit: Lower-severity citation defect: the quote used to support this claim is 'Hosta sieboldiana green' — RHS's listed synonym string — which does not itself assert that 'Hosta sieboldiana' is the accepted name; it only sounds related. The raw RHS page actually contains a directly on-point structured field the record didn't cite: 'Name Status: Correct.' The underlying value (accepted name unchanged from given name) still checks out against both MOBOT and RHS, so this is a citation-support weakness rather than a wrong value.

outdoor_sun_exposure — removed on audit: The record includes "part_shade" based on prose from NC State ("prefers full sun to light shade") and Missouri Botanical Garden ("Tolerates ... some light shade"). But on both of those same pages, the source's own STRUCTURED cultural-conditions field disagrees with its own prose: NC State's structured 'Light:' field (a controlled-vocabulary dt/dd pair separate from the free-text 'Description' paragraph) contains only a single value -- 'Full sun (6 or more hours of direct sunlight a day)' -- with no Part Shade/Partial Shade tag present anywhere on the page (verified directly against the page's raw HTML; the word 'shade' appears only inside the unstructured Description paragraph). Likewise MOBOT's structured 'Sun:' row reads only 'Full sun', with the shade-tolerance language confined to the separate prose 'Culture' note. RHS and UGA -- the record's other two admissible sources for sun exposure -- state 'Full sun' with no shade mention at all. So every admissible source's own structured/controlled-vocabulary sun-exposure field says full sun only; 'part_shade' rests solely on softer narrative asides on two of those same pages that their own structured fields do not corroborate. This is the exact 'source's own structured fields contradict the prose quote' pattern that should have triggered caution (and at minimum a note of the conflict) rather than a clean two-source part_shade addition.

water_regime — removed on audit: The record set water_regime to "keep_moist" using two prose fragments (NC State: "Phlox needs to be watered in dry summers..."; MoBot: "Intolerant of drought and needs to be watered in dry spells"), but it ignored the Missouri Botanical Garden source's own STRUCTURED field for this exact page, which reads "Water: Medium" (verified directly in the live page HTML: "Sun: Full sun to part shade Water: Medium Maintenance: Medium"). MoBot's structured Water tag uses a scale (Dry / Medium / Medium to wet / Wet) where "Medium" denotes average garden watering, not the elevated, don't-let-it-dry-out regime "keep_moist" implies -- MoBot did not tag this plant Wet or Medium-to-wet despite writing 'intolerant of drought' in prose. NC State's own watering sentence is similarly mild ('needs to be watered in dry summers', i.e. supplemental water only during dry spells against a backdrop of otherwise-sufficient rainfall), not a statement that the plant must be kept continuously moist. Additionally, the NC State citation's quote splices in 'Overhead watering should be avoided,' which on the source page is advice about avoiding wet foliage to prevent powdery mildew, not a statement about soil moisture level, padding the citation with irrelevant text. This is exactly the pattern flagged by structural check #1: a cited source's own structured field (MoBot's 'Water: Medium') contradicts the more demanding prose-derived value the record actually selected, and the record picked a value anyway instead of settling on a more conservative/lower category or leaving water_regime null.

unknowns: toxic_to_pets / toxicity_detail: none of the admissible sources (RHS, NC State Extension, Clemson HGIC) address toxicity of P. rhoeas to pets or humans; non-admissible sites claim toxicity from isoquinoline alkaloids but cannot be used per the source-domain restriction.
direct_sun_hours_max: NC State defines full sun as '6 or more hours of direct sunlight a day' — an open-ended minimum, not an upper bound, so no max value can be recorded.

soil_ph_min / soil_ph_max: NC State lists all three pH categories (Acid <6.0, Neutral 6.0-8.0, Alkaline >8.0) as acceptable and RHS says 'Acid or Alkaline or Neutral' — both indicate broad tolerance rather than a specific recommended numeric range.

water_regime: no source phrases watering in terms of a dry-down/moisture regime; NC State's 'fertile, medium moist, well-drained soils' describes a preferred planting site, not a watering schedule instruction.

water_check_depth_cm / water_dry_down_target / water_estimate_basis / water_growing_days_est / water_dormant_days_est: no admissible source gives watering frequency, depth, or schedule data for this outdoor annual.

day_f_min/max, night_f_min/max: no admissible source gives daytime/nighttime temperature ranges; RHS only gives a winter cold-hardiness rating (H7, hardy to below -20C), which is a different kind of data.

chill_damage_f: no source gives a chill-injury threshold temperature; RHS's H7 hardiness rating describes extreme winter cold tolerance of the species as a whole, not a chill-damage threshold, so it is not used for this field.
cool_rest_note: no admissible source discusses a cool-rest or dormancy care note.
humidity_need / humidity_pct_min / humidity_pct_max: no admissible source discusses humidity requirements for this outdoor garden annual.
light_fc_min / light_fc_good: no source gives light levels in foot-candles; only 'full sun' position/hours language is given.
fertilize_active_months / fertilize_interval_days / fertilize_strength: no admissible source discusses a fertilizing schedule or strength for corn poppy.

soil_base — removed on audit: Live-fetched the NC State page: the cited quote ('Corn Poppy is best grown in fertile, medium moist, well-drained soils in full sun') describes soil composition and sun exposure only — it says nothing about garden bed vs. container cultivation. The claim's parenthetical ('grown directly in outdoor garden soil rather than a container or specialty mix') is an unsupported inference not derivable from that quote; corn poppy is in fact commonly grown in containers/window boxes as a bedding annual, so the explicit exclusion of containers is an over-reach beyond the cited source.

soil_drainage — removed on audit: Live-fetched both pages: NC State's structured value is literally 'Good Drainage' and RHS's is 'Well–drained' — both are qualitative descriptors meaning 'not waterlogged,' not statements about drainage rate/speed. Mapping either to a 'fast' drainage category is an interpretive leap the quotes don't establish; neither source uses language about quick/sandy-type drainage, so 'fast' over-specifies what the citations actually say.

is_houseplant is recorded false based on NC State's outdoor-only landscape uses; RHS's genus-level Horticultural Classification note says Primrose-group primulas may be 'grown as biennial container plants in greenhouses or indoors,' but this is a conditional, group-level remark (not specific to Primula vulgaris or to long-term indoor culture), so it was not treated as evidence of houseplant suitability.

soil_ph: NC State gives a specific numeric range ('Neutral (6.0-8.0)'), used for soil_ph_min/max. RHS separately gives a broader, non-numeric categorical range ('Acid or Alkaline or Neutral') for the same species — noted here as additional context since it has no number to reconcile against, not treated as a conflicting numeric claim.

Mature size/plant dimensions were not captured: NC State's structured height field ('0 ft. 3 in. - 6 ft. 0 in.') and RHS's ('Up to 10 cm' / description 'about 20cm tall') differ by roughly two orders of magnitude for what appears to be the same low rosette-forming species; there is no mature-size field in this schema, so this conflict did not need to be resolved, but it is flagged in case it matters elsewhere.

soil_ph_min — removed on audit: The record sets soil_ph_min=6.0 using only NC State's 'Neutral (6.0-8.0)' quote, but the record's own second cited source for this exact species page — RHS (https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/13901/primula-vulgaris-(pr-prim)/details) — directly fetched and confirmed states 'Soil pH: Acid or Alkaline or Neutral', i.e. RHS says P. vulgaris tolerates acidic and alkaline soil, not just the neutral 6.0-8.0 band NC State gives. This is a genuine cross-source disagreement on a harm-capable field (wrong pH guidance risks nutrient lockout/poor establishment). The record acknowledges the conflict in its own unknowns text but dismisses it as 'additional context... not treated as a conflicting numeric claim, since it has no number to reconcile against' and keeps NC State's narrower number anyway — this is exactly the 'conflict resolved by preference, not left null' defect pattern; RHS's categorical claim does conflict with the implied bounds of NC State's numeric claim and the field should have been left null or widened, not silently resolved in NC State's favor.

soil_ph_max — removed on audit: Same defect as soil_ph_min: soil_ph_max=8.0 is taken solely from NC State's 'Neutral (6.0-8.0)' while RHS's own page for the same species (fetched directly, not just the source proposing NC State's number) states the plant tolerates 'Acid or Alkaline or Neutral' soil pH, a materially broader/conflicting claim about the same harm-capable field that was downgraded to a footnote instead of causing the field to be nulled.

normalizations: 2026-08-21: Papaver rhoeas (Corn Poppy) was re-run as a small single-species retry before landing. Its first pass returned citations=null instead of an array -- a genuine schema violation the tool-calling validation didn't catch -- while still asserting two non-null field values (outdoor_sun_exposure, soil_drainage) with zero supporting evidence attached. The loader's own null-safety would have refused both silently and correctly, but reading the discarded record's 13 unknowns entries showed genuinely careful reasoning underneath (including the same correct genus-vs-species toxicity exclusion Hosta's record made), so a cheap 2-agent retry (139K tokens against the batch's usual ~1.7M) recovered the work properly rather than losing it or landing an evidence-less record. The retry's own audit caught two further overreaches: soil_base wrongly excluded container growing, which corn poppy is commonly grown in; soil_drainage over-specified 'fast' from qualitative 'well-drained'/'Good Drainage' language neither source actually ties to drainage rate.

Hosta correctly left toxic_to_pets null despite being flagged in advance as commonly known toxic to cats -- the only admissible source discussing pet toxicity was a genus-level 'Hosta' overview covering all 22 species and 2000+ cultivars, never naming Hosta sieboldiana specifically, so the no-genus-inference rule held even against a flagged expectation. Hardy Geranium's own record explicitly recognized and excluded a genus mismatch: toxic-houseplant lists it found were about Pelargonium, the different genus popularly also nicknamed 'geranium', not Geranium sanguineum.
